A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EGENNET research. All 24 pages, including Appendices A–I, equations, figures and tables, are available for comparison; the image-based Table 6 is also readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original EGENNET separation experiments and chemical-property prediction results in Section 6 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains the original EGENNET separation and chemical-property prediction results, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The aggregation equations, invariant readout and node/edge-feature extension in Appendix H are unchanged. Explicitly describing the readout matrix theta as learnable clarifies the existing architecture rather than changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pair a/b, 4- and 12-chain graphs, four challenging point-cloud pairs, and the Drugs, Kraken and BDE chemical-property tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–6, including SchNet variants, DimeNet and SphereNet in the power-graph comparisons, the equivariant k-chain baselines, and the chemistry and hard-example baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain the same protocols, including the 70/10/20 chemistry split, MAE evaluation, 1,500 training epochs, model configurations and synthetic graph/depth settings.

E4.justification: The power-graph comparisons in Table 1, depth analyses in Tables 3–4 and challenging point-cloud cases in Table 5 are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten seeds for power-graph and k-chain experiments and three seeds for chemistry, with the same best-validation-seed selection and mean/standard-deviation reporting. Appendix I's changed table reference is an editorial inconsistency, not evidence of a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: All six tables retain their result entries, including the identical image-based Table 6. For example, both versions report EGENNET's BDE MAE as 0.3170 in Table 2 and 100% accuracy at seven layers for 12-chains in Table 4.

T1.justification: After Corollary 5.2, v2 adds a cited embedding-dimension lower bound of nd - d(d-1)/2 and an argument that its 2nd+1 dimension is optimal within a factor of two when n is much larger than d. Existing theorem statements and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: connectivity characterizes generic E-GGNN separation, global rigidity characterizes I-GGNN separation, and EGENNET achieves generic maximal expressivity with competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the existing embedding dimension as approximately optimal using the added lower-bound comparison. Interpretations of the experiments, the over-squashing suggestion and limitations concerning symmetric or non-generic inputs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository URL in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Appendix B's implementation instructions, hyperparameters, software and hardware information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds two unresolved MPNN citation keys in Section 2 and newly relates its embedding dimension to a lower bound attributed to reference [50]. The numbered bibliography and Appendix A's related-work discussion are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammar, terminology and notation clarifications while retaining the document's structure. It also introduces a visible 'TODO - add description' in Section 6.2 and incorrectly changes Appendix I's reference to the main-text results from Table 2 to Table 6.

P2.justification: Table 1 shifts lower on page 8, and Table 2 moves from preceding Section 6.2 to following its discussion. Equation numbering and page reflow also change, but both figures and all table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful code-access information, explanatory clarifications and embedding-dimension context. However, it introduces unresolved citations, a visible TODO and an incorrect table reference that obscures the distinction between selected-seed and averaged results. With the empirical evidence and core proofs unchanged, these modest benefits and editorial regressions do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
